title: Lord Ganesh Scribes
intro: _This week, I would like to write about Lord Ganesh - that Wise, Benevolent Elephant-faced God who guards our road in life and removes obstacles before we get there. When I look upon His face in our own Sri Ganesh Mandir, His Broken Tusk reminds me of this story. My inner dialog is in Italics for you to ruminate on._
body: Long ago, Sage Vyasa classified the hymns recited by The Wise or The Gods into the Vedas. These were insights passed down for generations to allow humanity to flourish and lead happy, fulfilling lives. But they were too abstract for the human mind to comprehend and he was struck by an urge to write a story to simplify it and set examples to follow and avoid. He did not have to cast a wide net for a fitting story and characters. He chose his own family’s tale to prove that Jaya (victory) goes to Dharma (sacred duty).

_Golden words to follow in our life: hold your duty/job in life as sacred, pour yourself into it, and surely, Victory is marching your way. It may take time for Her to turn around a corner but keep the faith._

Sage Vyasa needed a scribe who could write as fast as his thoughts and poetry would flow. He also needed someone who was learned enough to stop and correct him or clarify/simplify if his words wandered into abstractness. Being one of the eldest, wisest sages, it was hard for any other human to fulfill this role. He searched far and wide and meditated to The Gods. Finally, The Gods answered with Lord Ganesh - the God of Wisdom and Intellect to serve humanity as Sage Vyasa’s scribe.

_In my role, I often have to ask clarifying/simplifying questions and provide more information to my leaders to make sure we are making a decision with all relevant information. The path of least resistance is sometimes to go with what the leaders say. But details, instinct, and experience can help us there, and a little confidence from Lord Ganesha, the Scribe, who kept Sage Vyasa in check._

Lord Ganesh descended to Sage Vyasa’s ashram with His trusted pen and papyrus. Sage Vyasa welcomed Him with a desk to write comfortably. Lord Ganesh’s one stipulation was that Sage Vyasa shall narrate without pausing so that he doesn’t add his own prejudices and flavors to the story. Sage Vyasa thought and requested that Lord Ganesh write a sentence only if it made perfect sense and He agreed with it. This ensured that divine intellect flowed into the story and gave Sage Vyasa time to organize his thoughts.

_A scribe is not a typist. Lord Ganesh did not just write down what Vyasa said. He added His intellect and insights. When I scribe meeting minutes, I do my part to detail critical actions and enablers to ensure we are moving along the critical path._

_I also notice that Sage Vyasa adds his checks and balances in this partnership. He curtails the flow of work with the balance of logic and intellect to ensure the end product is worthy. Every team member has a role to fulfill and a good understanding of roles and motivations of the team member is critical for progress with harmony._

Thus began the saga of a hundred thousand verses that Sage Vyasa recited and Lord Ganesh scribed non-stop. As He wrote, His pen broke. But Vighnaharta Ganesh (Remover of Obstacles) wouldn’t let this small detail pause this great endeavor or break His promise to write non-stop. He broke His tusk nonchalantly, dipped it in ink, and continued to write. Thus, He added one more name for His worshippers to call Him - Ekadantha: The One who doesn’t hesitate to sacrifice His tusk to continue the good work.

_Ganesha stands here as an example of finding a way when circumstances are against you and knowing that if you are going down the right path and obstacles present themselves, there are people and Ganesha around you to help._

**This partnership resulted in the great epic Mahabharatha that has been passed down for eons and retold countless times to teach Purushartha (meaning of human existence) which has four aspects, all important to lead a happy life.**
